source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: The only freedom which deserves the name, is that of pursuing our own good in our own way, so long as we do not attempt to deprive others of theirs, or impede their efforts to obtain it. Each is the proper guardian of his own health, whether bodily, or mental and spiritual.

author.name: John Stuart Mill
author.heading: About John Stuart Mill
author.metaLine: 1806–1873 · English philosopher, political economist & Member of Parliament
author.bio: John Stuart Mill was the leading English-language liberal philosopher of the nineteenth century and a founding figure of modern utilitarianism. His 1859 essay On Liberty argues that the only warrant for society to coerce an individual is to prevent harm to others — the “harm principle.” This line is the essay’s clearest statement of that ideal.

misattribution.heading: A note on how it’s quoted
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Mill is correct — this is a rare case where the famous name really did write the famous line. The only thing worth flagging is how the sentence is usually trimmed.

items.why: The widely shared version ends at “…deprive others of theirs,” dropping Mill’s closing clause “or impede their efforts to obtain it.” The primary text shows the full sentence.

misattribution.truthLine: Genuinely Mill, genuinely from On Liberty (1859), Chapter I — the popular form simply stops a clause early.

context.heading: Why it matters
lead: This sentence is the emotional core of Mill’s “harm principle”: the idea that each person should be free to live by their own conception of the good, limited only by the equal freedom of others. It is one of the most-quoted formulations of liberal individualism in the English language.

Because the line is so quotable, it usually circulates in a shortened form that stops at “…deprive others of theirs.” That truncation is faithful to Mill’s meaning — but his actual sentence adds a further clause about not impeding others’ efforts, and continues into a discussion of each person as “the proper guardian of his own health.”
